newsitem.title: INDIA: India police say six militants shot dead in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: India police say six militants shot dead in Kashmir.

text.p: Six separatist guerrillas were killed in a gunbattle in India's northern of state Jammu and Kashmir, a senior Indian police officer said on Thursday.

"Last evening six suspected foreign militants were killed in an encounter which lasted almost six hours with B.S.F. (Border Security Forces)," Gurbachan Jagat, Director General of Jammu and Kashmir police told a news conference.
Indian authorities say Pakistan trains and arms foreign mercenaries and Kashmiri militants. Islamabad says it offers only political and diplomatic support to the separatists.
Nine separatist guerrillas were killed on Monday by Indian paramilitary troops in two different shootouts, police said.
The latest killings took place at Sangeenpora, a small hamlet on the outskirts of Anantnag town, 55 km (30 miles) south of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
Police and hospitals say over 20,000 people have been killed in insurgency related violence since 1990 in Jammu and Kashmir, India's only Moslem majority state.
On Thursday, all newspapers in Kashmir suspended publication for three days in protest against alleged human rights violations by Indian security forces.

"All newspapers published from Kashmir valley have decided to suspend their publications for three days in protest against human rights violations in Kashmir by security forces," a statement from Kashmir Press said. Kashmir Press is an association of editors of Valley based newspapers.

Over a dozen Kashmiri newspapers, most of them Urdu language papers, have stopped publication several times in the past to protest against curbs imposed on them by government and the militants since the rebellion broke out in 1990.
This is the first time they have halted the printing presses to protest against human rights violations.
Shops and schools remained closed a fourth day on Thursday in response to a strike called by separatists protesting against alleged human rights violations.
Dozens of guerrilla groups are fighting India's rule in Jammu and Kashmir seeking the state's merger with neighbouring Pakistan or independence.
